title.narrative: PERFORMANCE-BASED PARTNERSHIP SCHEME FOCUSING ON QUALITY PROGRAMMING, UNDERSTANDING CHANGE AND RESULTS FOR POOR HOUSEHOLDS AND COMMUNITIES

description.narrative: The REGRADE-II programme will work in North and Central Gondar, Amhara State, Ethiopia. It aims to contribute to Concern Ethiopia’s Green Graduation thematic programme, and the goal of the grant is to ensure households can sustainably meet their basic needs and have improved coping strategies through strengthened livelihoods which place value on the natural environment. The programme will support over 38,470 people living in extreme poor households, female headed households, households with disabled members, landless, older people. This will be done through households receiving monthly income support to meet their basic consumption needs, households have access to basic services through regular coaching visits and referral linkage to services and target communities have improved knowledge and practice on (AMIYCN) adolescent, maternal, infant, young and child nutrition, hygiene and sanitation through coaching visits and health system strengthening.. OVERALL COUNTRY PROG: To save lives, alleviate suffering and maintain human dignity among children under five (U5), and pregnant and lactating women (PLW) in Somali Region, Ethiopia.. SPECIFIC OUTCOME: RM Biodiversity 1: the programme aims to improve land management through employing integrated community based participatory watershed management, implementing bio-physical soil and water conservation measures RM Adaptation 2: This allocation will fund activities designed to promote community adaptation to climate change within targeted micro-watersheds. This will include physical and biological soil and water conservation activities aimed at rehabilitant of water and land resources that have been degraded by drought increase weather variability and over exploitation. Activities will include construction of stone-faced hillside terrace, eyebrow basins and the planting of native tree seedlings. RM Desertification 1: The programme sensitises participants every year during the appropriate agricultural season on the importance of greening their environment for soil and water conservation, improve the vegetation cover with multipurpose plants to rehabilitate degraded lands and obtain ecological benefits and mitigate the shocks due to climate change. DRR 1: Green Graduation programmes are intended to build the resilience of communities and natural systems to a changing climate through awareness raising, capacity building, environmental awareness and promoting climate-smart activities.Aid to Environment 1: Concern’s Green Graduation programme added a 5th pillar to the traditional graduation model - the ‘green’ aspect which aims to improve environmental protection and stability through awareness raising, capacity building, assessing environmental impacts, reducing and managing environmental risks and increasing natural assets.Capacity Building 1: building the capacity of communities on climate-smart activities is necessary for environmental protection and sustainability.Gender Equality 1: a gender lens is applied at every stage and a gender transformative approach is taken to tackle harmful gender norms, attitudes and practices.Nutrition 1: Through improved agricultural practices (increasing yields) and messaging on nutrition, the nutritional status of HHs is improved.
